secondaryIdInfos.domain: Austrian Breast and Colorectal Cancer Study Group

identificationModule.briefTitle: Study to Determine Treatment Effects of Denosumab in Patients With Breast Cancer Receiving Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multi-Centre Phase 3 Study to Determine the Treatment Effect of Denosumab in Subjects With Non-Metastatic Breast Cancer Receiving Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy.

armGroups.label: Denosumab
armGroups.description: Participants received 60 mg denosumab subcutaneous injection once every 6 months. All participants continued to receive an approved non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy.

armGroups.label: Placebo
armGroups.description: Participants received placebo subcutaneous injection once every 6 months. All participants continued to receive an approved non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy.

armGroups.label: SubStudy: Zoledronic Acid
armGroups.description: Eligible participants who completed the open-label phase could be enrolled into the zoledronic acid substudy and randomized to receive a single 5 mg intravenous dose of zoledronic acid 8 months after the last open-label dose of denosumab.

armGroups.label: Substudy: Standard of Care
armGroups.description: Eligible participants who completed the open-label phase could be enrolled into the zoledronic acid substudy and randomized to receive standard of care 8 months after the last open-label dose of denosumab.

interventions.name: Non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy
interventions.description: An approved non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor therapy (eg, anastrazole) in the adjuvant setting

interventions.name: Zoledronic Acid
interventions.description: 5 mg zoledronic acid administered at a constant infusion rate

interventions.name: Standard of Care
interventions.description: Standard of care (SoC) as recommended by the treating physician, depending on individual factors such as bone density, lifestyle recommendations by the Investigator such as diet, physical activities and sun exposure, as well as local treatment standards.
